Four additions in one release: databases are dumped before every backup, ZFS datasets are a backup type of their own, BombVault tells you when a backup looks wrong and not only when it fails, and an AI assistant can read your backup status and start a backup through the built-in MCP server.

## ✨ Added

### Automatic database dumps

- **Recognised databases are dumped before each backup.** PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB containers from the official images, PostGIS, TimescaleDB, pgvector, pgautoupgrade, Immich's database images, linuxserver, yobasystems and jc21 MariaDB and Oracle's mysql-server get a full SQL dump taken from the running server. It streams straight into the repository as a restore point of its own, so no dump file is written to appdata or anywhere else. Containers that only look like a database get the same switch on their card, off until you turn it on.
- **On by default.** Existing installations start dumping their recognised databases with the next backup, and the Containers page says how many there are. Switch it off per container on its card, with the label `bombvault.dbdump=false`, or for everything under Settings, General.
- **A failed dump never fails the backup.** It appears as a failed "Database dump" run with its reason and a hint how to fix it, counts on the dashboard and on the coverage card until it works again, shows up in the Unraid dashboard widget and in the metrics, and sends a notification (folded into the summary when you use summary mode).
- **No secret leaves the container.** The dump reads the container's own variables inside the container, including `_FILE` secrets and linuxserver's `FILE__` variables. BombVault never reads or stores a database password.
- **A truncated dump cannot become a restore point.** restic only keeps the dump when the dump tool exited cleanly, the end-of-dump marker is there and the stored size matches what was dumped.
- **You see what each dump holds.** The Backups panel lists every dump with its database version, the databases in it and its size.
- **Dumps are never loaded back on their own.** Download one as `.sql` or `.sql.gz`, save it to a folder, or import it into a freshly started database with one click, which keeps the old data folder next to it.
- **Each database shows how its data is covered.** Its card says whether the data folder is saved with the container stopped, copied while it runs (compose stacks), or not saved at all, and it warns before you switch off a dump that is the only consistent copy.
- **`DB_DUMP_MAX_HOURS`** (6 by default) bounds a single dump, and a dump that stops making progress is cut earlier.

### ZFS datasets

- **A ZFS page.** Pick a dataset from the server's list and it is backed up together with every dataset below it, all read from one ZFS snapshot, so every file comes from the same moment. New child datasets join on their own and the next backup names them. You can leave single children out.
- **Nothing is skipped silently.** A dataset that cannot be read (not mounted, key not loaded, never mounted) is skipped and named on the run, on the item and on the dashboard's coverage card.
- **Volumes are not part of it.** A volume a VM uses is backed up with that VM. A volume without a VM is counted on the page and not backed up; a later version will take care of those too.
- **Stored like a folder.** Each dataset is read from the ZFS snapshot and stored with restic, so unchanged data is not stored twice, every backup can be browsed and single files come back on their own. BombVault never uses `zfs send` for datasets.
- **Consistent apps without long downtime.** Name containers to stop just for the snapshot, or run a command before it. The stopped containers are back within seconds, and the backup reads the snapshot while they run.
- **Restores that never roll back.** Restore one dataset into its place, into a folder, or only the files you pick, or every dataset of a backup into a folder. Before writing into a dataset BombVault takes a ZFS safety snapshot (on by default), which stays until you delete it on the page. A dataset is never rolled back or replaced.
- **No leftover snapshots.** A snapshot BombVault could not remove after a backup is removed before the next one and when BombVault starts, and the page shows any that are still there. Containers left stopped by an interrupted snapshot are started again when BombVault starts.
- **Everywhere the other types are.** Schedules and per-item schedules, per-item repositories, retention, off-site copies (immutable too), drills, Backup Everything, coverage, metrics, Healthchecks per type, notifications, anomaly detection, the MCP server, the support bundle and the recovery kit all include ZFS datasets.

### Anomalies

- **Every backup is compared with its own history.** That covers each container, VM, folder set, database dump, ZFS dataset, the flash drive and the self-backup. Reported: much more new data than usual, most of the data stored again, a source or dump that is suddenly almost empty or much smaller, far fewer files, a much slower restic run, repeated or intermittent failures, a restore check that stopped passing, and a disk that will be full soon.
- **A ZFS item is checked dataset by dataset**, so a child dataset that was emptied shows even in a large tree.
- **Existing installs do not start from zero.** Sizes, file counts and restic durations are read once from the snapshots restic 0.17 already stores.
- **Old backups are kept when data is lost.** When a source shrinks sharply, or one backup stores most of the data again, BombVault keeps the old backups of that item, dump or dataset until you acknowledge the anomaly, so an emptied or encrypted folder cannot push the good backups out one night at a time. The anomaly links to the last good backup, and the restore panel marks the backup it was raised on.
- **Where you see it.** A dashboard card, an Anomalies page right under Dashboard in the sidebar with filters and bulk acknowledge, a badge and a learning indicator on every item, a mark on the runs in the history and the activity log, and a card on Settings, Integrity for the sensitivity (Strict, Balanced, Permissive) and the notification minimum, which each item can override.
- **Notifications for critical anomalies**, sent once per episode through the channels you already use. Which severities notify is configurable.
- **Backups record restic's own totals** (source size, file count, duration) per run.

### MCP server for AI assistants

- **An assistant can read how your backups are doing:** status per domain, coverage, the protected items with their last backup and what a backup of them stops, run history, restore points including database dumps and ZFS datasets, current activity, repository growth and the open anomalies.
- **With a key that allows it, it can start** a backup of one item, of one domain or Backup Everything, and cancel the backups its own key started. Restores, deletions, prune, acknowledging anomalies, settings, credentials and keys stay in the web interface.
- **One key per client**, created under Settings, System, MCP server, shown once and stored as a fingerprint, with read-only keys for clients you trust less. Every key change sends a notification.
- **Limits that protect your restore points:** 12 starts per hour per key, 15 minutes between starts of the same item, 4 per item a day, and a retention guard that keeps assistant backups from pushing your own restore points out of a "keep last N" policy.
- **You see what it did.** Every run it starts, and the prune and off-site copy that follow, reads "via MCP" with the key's name in the activity log, the error panel and the backup notification.
- **Works on a plain Unraid install.** The card adds the address you use to the self-signed certificate with one click and hands you the certificate file for the client. A reverse proxy or Tailscale works as well. The endpoint `/mcp` answers 404 until a key exists.

### Recovery kit and support bundle

- **The recovery kit covers all four.** It has the restic commands for getting a dump or a ZFS dataset back without BombVault, warns against restoring the newest snapshot after data loss (it can be the emptied or encrypted one), and says that restoring the settings backup revokes every MCP key.
- **The support bundle** carries the dump state of every database, the ZFS items and the mounts the container sees, the open anomalies and the number of MCP keys, never their names.
- **Settings export and import** carry the dump switch, the ZFS settings and the anomaly settings. A file from an older version leaves dumps, detection and the pause on old backups switched on.

## ⚡ Improved

- **The sidebar lists what needs looking at first:** Dashboard, Anomalies, then every backup type including ZFS, then Recovery and the other instances.
- **The template's SSH fields are now called Host SSH: Address, Port and User**, because VM and ZFS dataset backups both use them. Your values stay.
- **The address placeholder no longer blocks the connection.** With the address still at the template's `192.168.x.x`, BombVault tries the server itself through host.docker.internal.
- **A failed retention step also notifies when the notification policy was never set**, as it counted as "failures only" everywhere else already.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **TrueNAS: SSH commands went to the wrong machine.** When `LIBVIRT_URI` is set and the SSH host, user or port is not, BombVault takes each missing one from the URI for its own SSH commands as well, so the NVRAM transfer and ZFS commands reach the machine `virsh` talks to.
- **VM backups with zvol disks count the disks' new data in the run's size.**
- **Off-site copies from a named repository would have skipped dumps.** The copy is narrowed to the domain's snapshots, and that narrowing knows about dumps.
- **Tags reserved for BombVault can no longer be added by hand** to a snapshot, where they would have put it into an item's retention series or its dump list.
- **Successful runs with a note** (a restore that skipped paths, a dump of a single database) show that note in the run history.

## 🌐 Translations

- Every new screen, card, hint and message in all 42 languages, with the plural forms each language uses for counts.
- The MCP page of the documentation in all 26 documentation languages.

## 📝 Notes

- ZFS datasets need the SSH link to this server that VM backups use, and the Host Data path mapped as `/mnt` with Access Mode Read/Write - Slave (the template default).
- On TrueNAS, set the app's Host Data to a host path above the datasets, for example `/mnt/tank`.
- Anomaly detection learns from 10 backups per item. An almost empty source, a backup that stored most of the data again and failures are checked from the first one.
